name: DISTFLASHATTN: Distributed Memory-efficient Attention for Long-context LLMs Training
problem: Training long-context LLMs needs the attention computation sharded across devices, and existing approaches pay for it either in sequence-length limits (attention must be exact per sequence) or in imbalance and redundant communication.
mechanism: DISTFLASHATTN combines FlashAttention's tiling with sequence-level parallelism plus three named techniques: token-level workload balancing (so all devices finish together), overlapping key-value communication with compute, and a rematerialisation-aware gradient checkpointing algorithm. Same LightSeq codebase lineage as Sequence Level Parallelism.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), each against a NAMED distributed baseline, on Llama-7B at sequence lengths 32K-512K: 4.45-5.64x vs Ring Self-Attention (also 8x longer sequences); 1.24-2.01x vs Megatron-LM with FlashAttention (2-8x longer sequences); 1.67x vs recent Ring Attention; and 1.26-1.88x vs DeepSpeed-Ulysses. This is the best-baselined attention record in the batch - four named competitors, a model and a length range.
